correctness.rationale: For sample size four, independent derivation of the Okolewski–Papadatos generator moment equations gives m=(3c+2b)/S, v=(9ac−4b²)/S², S=3a+4b+3c. Equality gives zero variance and unique point generator, hence unique two-point parent with p=√c/(√a+√c), x=β1−a^(3/2)/(4√c), y=β4+c^(3/2)/(4√a). Strict feasibility gives 0<v<m(1−m); for u in (v/(1−m),m), r=m−u,s=m+v/u,w=v/(u²+v) realize same mean/variance as distinct two-point generators, whose explicit three-point parent inverse yields required four order means. Independently computed an interior example a=b=c=1 and constructed three-point law with expectations (0,1,2,3) to 5.3e−16. This bounded test corroborates, while source bijection and algebra prove continuum.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: This is precisely a truncated moment determinacy question. A two-moment law on (0,1) is uniquely a point mass when variance zero and nonunique whenever variance is strictly positive and below m(1-m). That fact is standard and, with the source map, entails exactly the claimed identification dichotomy.
